pages.page_title: w sprawie potencjalnych konfliktów interesów w Komisji Kodyfikacyjnej Prawa Cywilnego
pages.capture_answer: Signatory: Arkadiusz Myrcha, Sekretarz Stanu, for the Ministry of Justice. Date: Warszawa, 29 września 2025 r., reference BK-VII.0520.299.2025. The reply answers interpellation no. 11127 by MPs Anna Gembicka and Jarosław Sachajka on conflicts of interest in the Civil Law Codification Commission (KKPC). Amounts are per role, not per person: a monthly flat-rate remuneration of 10 000 zł for the chair, 8 500 zł for the deputy chair and 3 500 zł for a member, set in § 13 ust. 1 of the regulation (the 2002 Council of Ministers regulation, cited as Dz.U. z 2024 r. poz. 1447). The reply does not say how the chair is appointed. The only named individual payment is Marek Miller's waived remuneration. The reply gives no cost totals and no 2025 figures, and KKUSiP is not mentioned. Krystian Markiewicz, Maciej Taborowski and Marcin Dziurda do not appear, and no member list is given. The reply states there is no legal duty for members to declare whom they serve, and that members must withdraw where there is a conflict-of-interest risk. The reply refers to the Prime Minister and the Minister of Justice by office only; it does not name Donald Tusk or Waldemar Żurek. None of the other listed actors or NGOs appear.

followup_urls.why: Ministry page where, per the reply, Commission plenary-session information is published from 27 November 2024. The PDF text runs 'kodyfikacyjnaprawa' together and ends in a footnote digit, so the exact address is unverified. Not fetched.

pages.page_title: Ujawniamy kulisy odwołania zastępcy RPO. Partyjny deal w instytucji, która powinna być niezależna
pages.capture_answer: Deputy removed: dr hab. Adam Krzywoń, deputy Ombudsman. The new Ombudsman is Sylwia Gregorczyk-Abram. The only party named in the visible text is Lewica. The standfirst says Anna Maria Żukowska of Lewica confirms that dr Michał Peno will take the post on the club's recommendation, and the body has the line 'Lewica musi mieć swojego rzecznika'. KO, Polska 2050, PSL and PiS are not named in the visible text. Peno is described as a former Unia Pracy politician who has so far worked in the justice ministry; no appointment date is given for him. Dates: the RPO office announced on 9 października that Friday was Krzywoń's last working day, and the article is dated 11 października 2026. The 'party deal' is alleged by unnamed RPO office staff, who also say Gregorczyk-Abram was to tell Krzywoń she was dismissing him. The office says it did not dismiss him and that they parted by mutual agreement, and that personnel decisions rest on merit. Gregorczyk-Abram denies the nomination is political. OKO.press says the office's reply conflicts with its findings. The rest of the article is paywalled.

pages.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs Republic of Poland
pages.capture_answer: Answered from the page. Dated 02.03.2026, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs page says the government announced the nomination of Prof. Wojciech Sadurski and Prof. Monika Florczak-Wątor as new Polish representatives to the Venice Commission, and that the newly appointed experts 'will serve as members', so neither is described as a substitute. The steps it gives are national government nomination and approval by the Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe for a four-year term; the page does not say that approval was given to these two. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski said the decision was taken 'together with the Ministry of Justice'. Justice Minister Waldemar Żurek is quoted on the candidates' standards and independence. The page gives no party for Sikorski or Żurek. Sadurski is a professor of law at the University of Sydney and at the Centre for Europe at the University of Warsaw. Florczak-Wątor is a professor at the Jagiellonian University, and her work 'focuses on' the functioning of the Constitutional Tribunal, but the page names no Tribunal post, contract or fee for her. The page names no ISP, Batory Foundation, Osiatyński Archive or KOD tie for either nominee, and no fee or payment. Prof. Hanna Suchocka is named as a previous Polish representative. The ISP and IACL items were not linked from this page and were not read.

pages.capture_answer: Judges' assemblies across Poland gave opinions on 60 KRS candidates, each judge casting up to 15 votes; turnout about 60%. All 15 places went to the 'rule-of-law list': Zawistowski 4201, Jefimko 3587, Frąckowiak 3583, Bąk-Lasota 3537, Zawiślak 3536, Mierzejewska 3474, Kierszka 3405, Łuczaj 3394, Żołnierczuk-Dec 3386, Buchajczuk (Iustitia vice-president) 3382, Starosta 3363, Cilulko 3358, Wrzesińska-Nowacka 3355, Donhoffner-Grodzicka (Themis board) 3297, Kobylińska-Bortkiewicz 3289. Ziobro-era candidates: Radzik 14, Piebiak 39, Schab 34, Dudzicz 33, Zdun 54, Czubik 66, Dalkowska 86. The Sejm was to elect the judge-members soon, as the neo-KRS term ended in May 2026.

pages.page_title: Nowi sędziowie KRS wybrani przez Sejm. Wśród nich współpracownik Ziobry
pages.capture_answer: On Friday 15 May 2026 the Sejm elected 15 judge-members of the KRS (235 for, 18 against, 5 abstaining; 3/5 majority of 155; PiS MPs did not vote, citing a TK injunction of 12 May). 13 were named by the ruling coalition's clubs after the judges' assemblies' opinion vote, in which judges backed by associations including Iustitia and Themis won most support. The other two: Łukasz Piebiak (PiS pick, ex-deputy justice minister under Ziobro) and Łukasz Zawadzki (Konfederacja pick), both linked to Stowarzyszenie Prawnicy dla Polski. Of the assemblies' top 15, Sławomir Cilulko and Themis board member Beata Donhoffner-Grodzicka are not on the elected list.

The list was published on the Forum Współpracy Sędziów website after the Sejm resolution of 27 Feb 2026; the article gives no internal Iustitia selection procedure. 'Administarcyjnych' is a misspelling on the page, kept as written. Roles are stated for 8 of the 15; none is said to be delegated to the Justice Ministry.
pages.page_title: Lista 15 sędziów do KRS rekomendowanych przez niezależnych sędziów [NAZWISKA]
pages.capture_answer: A 15-judge candidate list for the renewed KRS, published on the Forum Współpracy Sędziów site, backed by the Family Judges' Association, the National Association of Administrative Court Judges, Themis and Iustitia. Stated roles: Buchajczuk, Iustitia vice-president for finance; Starosta, Iustitia member; Frąckowiak, linked to Iustitia and MEDEL, court president after PiS lost power; Donhoffner-Grodzicka, Themis board; Wrzesińska-Nowacka, president of the administrative judges' association; Zawistowski, last chair of the pre-2018 KRS; Cilulko, vice-president of the Białystok Regional Court; Kierszka, disciplinary judge at the Gdańsk Court of Appeal. 13 of the 15 were elected by the Sejm on 15 May 2026 (P5).

pages.capture_answer: Primary statement from the National Prosecutor's Office. On 21 Apr 2026 it opened an investigation into the non-admission of four TK judges elected by the Sejm on 13 Mar 2026. The case has two threads: (a) suspected aiding of the President's failure to fulfil his duties, i.e. not receiving the oaths (art. 18 §3 with art. 231 §1); (b) suspected failure of duty by public officials employed at the TK, who did not give the judges working conditions, pay, cases or employment formalities (art. 231 §1 and art. 218 §1a with art. 11 §2). The basis was a verification proceeding under Prosecutor General Waldemar Żurek's order of 13 Apr 2026, plus a criminal notification filed by TK judges Magdalena Bentkowska and Dariusz Szostek. Signed by prosecutor Anna Adamiak, press spokesperson of the Prosecutor General. No suspect is named.

pages.page_title: 10. kadencja, 63. posiedzenie, 3. dzień (31-07-2026)
pages.capture_answer: Account by Czesław Mroczek, Secretary of State at MSWiA, in the Sejm on 31 Jul 2026. Police acted on a report that two TK judges due at a planned TK General Assembly were not let into the building. They contacted the prosecutor's office at once, and officers and a prosecutor went to the TK only to establish the facts. The TK chancellery director and the TK guard commandant said they were carrying out the TK President's written order not to admit the judges. At the prosecutor's request they handed over a copy, and the judges complied. The prosecutor announced witness summonses and had police send the documentation to the National Prosecutor's Office. The TK President asked the Chief Commander of Police for the legal basis, and the Chief Commander replied.

Footnote 47 records the President's oath refusals, and the TK budget rose for 2026.
